notes:
Prospect: Peregrine Defence Comms – national-level contact center contractor supporting critical infrastructure incident response.

Key context:
- Must be deployed inside government-owned data center; strict air-gapped posture — "no egress" is non-negotiable (quote from CTO: "No external network calls during operations.").
- Primary workloads: agent-assist for live voice + screen-pop, automated ticket summarization (multi-channel), secure tool-calling into legacy ticketing system (SOAP/SSH gateway), and automated routing failover during peak incidents.
- Latency/throughput targets: median gen latency <= 150ms token for agent assist; 99th percentile conversational turn < 1.2s when under normal load; need deterministic behavior under spikes up to 3x baseline.
- Cost sensitivity: lower priority than security and reliability, but want Optimize guidance for quantization/batching to reduce GPU footprint inside air-gapped cluster.
- Model preferences: prefer vetted open weights that can be loaded inside air-gapped environment (customer asked about quantized Llama-family and Redwood-verified smaller models). No generative API egress allowed.
- Tool-calling: must support function/tool calling pattern but executed locally via hardened gateway to legacy ticket system; require allowlist and audit trails for each call.
- Compliance: require SOC2-like controls, ISO27001 evidence, audit-log retention for 7+ years, HSM-backed key management, and a FedRAMP-equivalent checklist (they are contracting via prime that requires gov-comparable controls).
- POC expectations: 2-week on-site air-gapped POC using 1 GPU rack to validate latency and failover, tape/USB delivery of model artifacts allowed after legal review.

Sales notes / dynamics:
- Procurement timeline tight: budget cycle Q2 2026, core decision team: CTO (security lead), Director of Ops (contact center), SRE lead.
- SE (Rohit) ran technical deep-dive on 2026-02-12 (see Fireflies ff_2026-02-12_0193). Security team pushed back on any option that requires outbound telemetry.
- Redwood differentiators that resonated: private on-prem bundle, HSM/KMS integration plan, Optimize recommendations for quantization and batching to meet deterministic latency targets.

Quote from Ops lead: "We need the system to act like an appliance — predictable latency during surges, and every function call auditable."

POC blockers: FedRAMP-equivalent attestation and statement of no-egress, legal signoff for on‑site model delivery, HSM integration runbook.

Next steps: 1) Deliver redlined FedRAMP-equivalent checklist by 2026-03-10; 2) Legal review of model transfer and NDA; 3) Schedule 2-week on-site POC week-of 2026-04-20 pending approvals.
